claude_proposed_widenings.name: world_state_control
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Control Weather's core mechanic is a staged world-state mutation: the caster shifts one of three weather axes (precipitation, temperature, wind) by ±1 on a DM-initialized discrete table, repeatably during concentration. No existing spell family can represent this. ongoing_effect requires a roll_modifier or damage_on_hit operation (neither applies). activation requires an attack_roll or save_gate phase (neither applies). triggered_reaction requires a Reaction casting time (casting time is 10 minutes). anchored_trigger requires an anchor point and event-triggered release (the spell actively grants ongoing control, not a stored trigger). A new family — world_state_control or environment_mutation — is needed for spells whose primary mechanic is steering a staged, DM-initialized environmental variable within a radius over a concentration duration.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: When you cast the spell, you change the current weather conditions, which are determined by the DM. You can change precipitation, temperature, and wind. [...] find a current condition on the following tables and change its stage by one, up or down.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: Range — self_radius_miles
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The spell's affected area is a 5-mile radius sphere centered on the caster. The existing Range union supports self (no extent), touch, and point (feet to target). A self-centered large-radius variant is needed — the sphere is fixed around the caster, not a targetable point. A point feet=26400 encoding would be dishonest about the geometry.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You take control of the weather within 5 miles of you for the duration.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: CastConstraint / cast_condition
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The spell requires the caster to be outdoors at cast time and terminates early if the caster goes indoors. No surface type models preconditions on the physical environment required for casting, or location-based early termination of a concentration effect. This is distinct from DurationExpiry (which is timed or concentration-based) — it is a circumstantial termination condition.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You must be outdoors to cast this spell, and it ends early if you go indoors.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: TransitionDelay
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: After the caster changes weather conditions, 1d4×10 minutes must pass before the new conditions take effect. No surface type models a random delay between a caster's in-spell action and its effect manifesting in the world. This is mechanically distinct from spell duration (the overall 8-hour window) and from casting time (10 minutes to initiate the spell).
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: It takes 1d4 × 10 minutes for the new conditions to take effect.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: modify_world_state
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The spell's entire effect output is shifting the stage of a discrete environmental variable (weather axis) within a large area. All v4 effect atoms target creatures, rolls, movement, or named effects on creatures/objects. No atom covers mutation of enumerable environmental/world-state stages. This is the primary effect atom the world_state_control family would grant.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: find a current condition on the following tables and change its stage by one, up or down. When changing the wind, you can change its direction.
